item.title: Live Operations Command Dashboard
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Running live classes across hundreds of batches meant the operations team was juggling spreadsheets, chat threads and manual reports. I designed a single command dashboard that pulls attendance, instructor status and open issues into one live view.

The problem

Issues were found late and tracked in too many places. Managers could not tell, at a glance, which classes were at risk.

What I built

  • A live timeline of every class with colour-coded status
  • Escalation counters that surface unresolved issues first
  • Daily and weekly trend views for attendance and incident rates

Result

Response time to class issues dropped sharply and the daily reporting routine went from hours to minutes.
item.excerpt:encoded: A real-time dashboard that gives the operations team one view of every live class, issue and escalation.

item.title: Survey Data Analysis in R
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
This project takes a raw survey export and walks it all the way to decisions: cleaning, coding, testing and visualising the results in R.

Approach

I cleaned and recoded the responses, checked assumptions, then used regression and group comparisons to find which factors actually moved the outcome.

Highlights

  • Reproducible R scripts from import to final charts
  • Boxplots and model summaries written for non-technical readers
  • A short findings brief with recommended actions

The output was a repeatable workflow the team could reuse for every new survey round.
item.excerpt:encoded: Turning raw survey responses into clean, tested insight with regression, group comparisons and clear visuals.

item.title: AI Assistant for Student Support
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Support and operations teams kept answering the same questions. I prototyped an AI assistant that answers them instantly from an approved knowledge base and hands off to a person when it is unsure.

Design goals

  • Answers grounded in approved documents only
  • Clear hand-off to a human for anything uncertain
  • Simple suggested questions to guide new users

Outcome

Repeat questions were handled automatically, freeing the team to focus on the cases that genuinely need a person.
item.excerpt:encoded: A conversational assistant that answers common student and operations questions from a trusted knowledge base.

item.title: Behind the Spotlight: What Running Live Class Operations Really Involves
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
When a live class starts on time and runs smoothly, nobody notices the operations behind it. That is exactly the point, and exactly the challenge.

Before the class

Schedules, instructor readiness, links and backups are checked well before learners join. Most problems are cheaper to fix an hour early than a minute late.

During the class

A live view of every session lets the team spot dropped connections or missing instructors immediately, and act before learners are affected.

After the class

Every issue is logged and reviewed. Patterns in that data decide what we fix permanently, not just patch.

Good operations is invisible: the best day is the one where nothing needs to be explained.
item.excerpt:encoded: Live classes look effortless from the outside. Here is the planning, monitoring and quick thinking that keeps them running.

item.title: Why I Chose Business Analytics: Turning Raw Survey Data into Insight
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Early in my career I noticed that the teams making the best decisions were not the ones with the most data, but the ones who asked the sharpest questions of it.

From data to decisions

Raw survey responses are noisy. Cleaning, structuring and testing them is where most of the value is created, long before any chart is drawn.

My simple process

  1. Start with the decision that needs to be made
  2. Clean and structure the data
  3. Test what actually matters
  4. Present it so anyone can act on it

That mix of operations experience and analytics is what I want to keep building.
item.excerpt:encoded: Numbers on their own do not change anything. Here is why I moved into analytics and how I approach turning data into decisions.

item.title: Joining the National Newspaper Olympiad as Chief Marketing Officer
item.dc:creator: admin
item.content:encoded:
Taking on the Chief Marketing Officer role for a national student event meant building a campaign, a team and a community at the same time.

What the role involved

Planning the campaign calendar, coordinating volunteers, and keeping partners and participants informed from announcement day to the final event.

What I learned

  • A clear message beats a big budget
  • Volunteers stay when they feel ownership
  • Measure early, adjust fast

Most of all, it reminded me that great results come from the people around you.
item.excerpt:encoded: What I learned leading marketing for a national student event, and the team that made it happen.
